answer: In an autonomous orchard network, Sybil resistance can rely on memory-bus contention profiling. When triggered by an audit pulse, an agent runs a cache-evicting kernel to measure physical DRAM latency under strict time limits. An attacker attempting to host multiple identities incurs the verifiable cost of dedicated physical memory buses per agent. However, adversaries using high-bandwidth memory can exploit channel parallelism to amortize hardware expenses.
